entries.mechanism: The description names chat_read among the product readers that could fail transiently on a torn line, but the chat_read tool never goes through _read_lines: it reads chat_reads.read_tail -> tail_rows, which splits on b'\n', skips unparseable lines and never raises, so it was never affected (the PR body's own 'other readers' list says tail_rows already skips). Motivation-only inaccuracy; the transcript route (hud_api.py:2242) and runner read_log (runner.py read_log callers) claims are correct.
entries.location: PR description ('a transcript route, chat_read or the runner's read_log could fail transiently'); jarvis/v2/tools/chats.py:142-158; jarvis/v2/chat_reads.py:254-286, 614-619
entries.evidence: traced: chat_read returns chat_reads.read_tail(service.stores, target, last) (tools/chats.py:158); read_tail calls tail_rows (chat_reads.py:619); tail_rows wraps reads in try/except and `continue`s on ValueError/UnicodeError (chat_reads.py:277-286). No read_log call on that path.

non_issues.claim: _read_lines should take _lock (or the reader is racy); tolerating a torn tail is papering over a race
non_issues.why_not: Lock-free reads are the stated design (docstring jarvis/v2/stores.py:104-112): only the last unterminated line can be in flight because _append writes whole lines under _lock (stores.py:242-258). The concurrent writer/reader test (tests/v2/stores_check.py torn_read part 6) passes on head and the torn_read test fails on base stores.py (verified: StoreError log.jsonl:3 Unterminated string). Taking the lock is an alternative, not a defect.

non_issues.claim: a torn last line that happens to parse returns a truncated or wrong record
non_issues.why_not: _append only writes one JSON object per line (stores.py:242-258, json.dumps(entry) of a dict); a proper prefix of a serialized object never parses, because the first depth-0 '}' is its last character. A complete record that only lacks its newline parses and is correctly returned; a non-object tail still raises (stores.py:142-143, test part 5).

non_issues.claim: callers that page by row index (transcript ?after=, task journal ?after=, the Discord mirror's len(read_log)) skip or repeat a record when a read leaves out the torn tail
non_issues.why_not: Only the final row can be omitted, so a read returns a prefix of the next read: counts are monotonic and the omitted record appears at the same index once its newline lands. No earlier row ever shifts.

non_issues.claim: a file ending in a bare '\r' is treated as newline-terminated, so a torn write ending at '\r' is reported as corruption
non_issues.why_not: No writer can stop at a raw CR: json.dumps escapes every control character below 0x20 even with ensure_ascii=False, and _append writes only '\n' (stores.py:242-258). UTF-8 multibyte sequences never contain 0x0A/0x0D.

non_issues.claim: the PR makes a crash-torn tail permanent: it is hidden until the next append, whose newline repair turns it into interior corruption that raises forever
non_issues.why_not: Pre-existing and not caused by the diff: base 8d73bead raises StoreError log:2 both before and after the next append (probe run in-process on base and head); head only stops raising while no further write happens. The newline repair in _append predates the PR. A daemon crash mid-append is the only way to leave such a tail (writes are under _lock).

non_issues.claim: the cut-multibyte branch can hide invalid UTF-8 elsewhere in the file, or mishandles a file with no newline at all
non_issues.why_not: bytes.decode reports the first error, so an earlier invalid byte gives a different reason ('invalid start byte'/'invalid continuation byte') and raises; tests/v2/stores_check.py:262-268 cover \xff terminated and unterminated and an earlier bad line before a cut character. With no newline rfind is -1, the slice is empty and the read is [] (probe: b'{"t": "\xe2\x9c' -> []).

non_issues.claim: other JSONL readers (chat_reads.tail_rows, SubagentStore._read) still fail on a torn line or split on U+2028
non_issues.why_not: Both split on b'\n' and skip any unparseable line, never raising (chat_reads.py:277-286, subagents.py:704-714). (migrate.py:49 still uses splitlines on a v1 log, but that is pre-existing, a one-time v1 import outside this diff, not a defect of this PR.)
